status_summary: EPA ended its environmental justice and DEI units on 2025-03-12, and its fiscal year 2026 reorganization addendum (September 2025) states that the Office of Environmental Justice and External Civil Rights and the ten regional environmental justice divisions were eliminated, with accessibility and external civil rights work moved to an Office of Civil Rights in the Administrator's office. The addendum also created an Office of Applied Science and Environmental Solutions, moved Office of Research and Development scientists into program offices, merged the Chief Financial Officer's office with most of the Office of Mission Support into an Office of Finance and Administration, and eliminated ten organizational units in the Office of Enforcement and Compliance Assurance. The Mandate called for eliminating that enforcement office and restructuring the Office of International and Tribal Affairs, but EPA's organization chart page (updated 2026-09-09) still lists both offices. EPA reported in July 2025 a workforce falling from 16,155 to 12,448; its budget page lists a fiscal year 2026 enacted workforce of 12,312, and the fiscal year 2027 request is $4.203 billion (52 percent below fiscal year 2026 enacted) with 12,500 FTE and up to $20 million to optimize office and laboratory space. No regional office relocation plan, General Counsel consolidation of enforcement attorneys, or tribal office restructuring was found.

timeline.event: EPA announces it will end its environmental justice and DEI units; staff are placed on administrative leave, and EPA ties the step to an executive order on DEI programs.

A nonprofit (PEER) files an administrative complaint with the Office of Special Counsel on behalf of the environmental justice staff on leave; a Harvard tracker also reports Zeldin ordered the closure of the Office of Environmental Justice and External Civil Rights and the ten regional EJ divisions (tracker dates are inconsistent, March 11 to April 11, 2025).
timeline.source: Harvard Environmental and Energy Law Program

timeline.event: EPA announces a next phase of reorganization: a new Office of Applied Science and Environmental Solutions in the Office of the Administrator, a new Office of State Air Partnerships and an Office of Clean Air Programs; EPA says staffing would return to levels near the Reagan era and savings would exceed $300 million a year by fiscal year 2026.

EPA announces a reduction in force affecting the Office of Research and Development, citing $748.8 million in savings and a workforce falling from 16,155 (January 2025) to 12,448; earlier it had ended EJ and DEI offices with 280 employees in a reduction in force and 195 transferred.

An EPA fiscal year 2026 budget addendum on consolidation and reorganization (month-level date from the file path, first of month used) describes eliminating the Office of Environmental Justice and External Civil Rights and the ten regional environmental justice divisions, creating the Office of Applied Science and Environmental Solutions, dissolving the Office of Research and Development's structure by moving scientists into program offices, merging the Chief Financial Officer's office with most of the Office of Mission Support into an Office of Finance and Administration, and eliminating ten units in the Office of Enforcement and Compliance Assurance, which is retained. It does not mention the international and tribal office or the General Counsel.

E&E News reported EPA is reducing office space at its Region 9 and Region 5 offices, which EPA called routine multi-year space management; this is a footprint change, not the regional relocation plan the Mandate describes.

EPA's fiscal year 2027 Budget in Brief (filed under April 2026, exact day not confirmed, first of month used) proposes $4.203 billion and 12,500 FTE, a 52 percent decrease from fiscal year 2026 enacted, continues realignments, and proposes up to $20 million to optimize office and laboratory space, including laboratory consolidation and releasing space in high-cost areas of regional offices.

EPA's organization chart page (last updated on this date) lists ten headquarters offices, including the Office of Enforcement and Compliance Assurance, the Office of Finance and Administration and the Office of International and Tribal Affairs, and does not list a stand-alone Office of Research and Development or American Indian Environmental Office.

title: Reorganize EPA: close environmental justice offices, restructure science, cut staff
uncertainties: The 16,155 baseline and 12,448 target come from EPA's July 2025 release (headcount), while the 14,130 and 12,312 budget-page figures are FTE ceilings, so they are not directly comparable. The fiscal year 2026 addendum and the 2026-04 Budget in Brief carry month-level dates only (taken from file paths). The addendum describes planned and completed changes without separate effective dates. The organization chart page lists only top-level offices, so the absence of the American Indian Environmental Office there is not proof it was abolished. A PEER complaint to the Office of Special Counsel on behalf of environmental justice staff is reported only by Harvard's tracker, whose dates are inconsistent. One web search for court challenges to EPA reductions in force returned no usable results, so litigation outcomes are unknown. Not verified: Office of Public Engagement, Children's Health Protection and Small and Disadvantaged Business Utilization changes, and any EPA statement on General Counsel consolidation.
